claims.claim: Identity and tradability are validated as Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE: CRM; CIK 0001108524). Current cumulative evidence resolves to two distinct issuer-origin fingerprints plus one independent current market-data origin; repeated issuer references are collapsed rather than counted as independent corroboration.

Primary operating evidence is current through 2026-09-10 and the independent valuation observation is current to September 2026; issuer-defined Agentforce ARR changed scope in Q2 FY27, so comparisons using that metric require definition-aware treatment.

risks.risk: Issuer-defined AI ARR changed scope in Q2 FY27 and acquisition contribution complicates organic comparisons.

unknowns.unknown: Independent corroboration is strong for current market value but limited for issuer-specific operating metrics; this reduces confidence rather than being treated favorably.

claims.claim: Q2 FY27 revenue was $11.3B (+11% YoY), subscription/support revenue $10.8B (+12%), cRPO $33.5B (+14% constant currency), GAAP operating margin 20.5%, operating cash flow $1.3B (+71%) and free cash flow $1.1B (+81%).
Agentforce and Data 360 ARR approached $3.9B (+210% YoY) and Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5B, but Q2 FY27 expanded the Agentforce ARR definition to include Slackbot and Headless 360.

FY27 revenue guidance of $46.1B-$46.4B implies 11%-12% growth but includes slightly above three points from Informatica and pending acquisitions; management attributed $100M of the guidance raise to organic growth.

September 2026 market evidence places CRM near a $196B-$200B market capitalization and roughly 27x trailing earnings, leaving plausible but not exceptional valuation headroom against double-digit reported growth and acquisition-adjusted uncertainty.

risks.risk: Acquisition contribution and changing AI metric definitions can make headline growth overstate directly comparable organic economics.
Agent value can migrate toward external model/orchestration layers if CRM context becomes portable.

contradictions.contradiction: Headline FY27 growth is 11%-12%, but guidance includes acquisition contribution and only $100M of the raise was described as organic.
contradictions.disposition: Explicitly reflected in financial momentum, valuation, risk and confidence rather than treated as organic growth.

unknowns.unknown: Agentforce-specific incremental gross margin, retention and organic economics remain undisclosed.
Current evidence does not demonstrate exceptional supply-chain redundancy because software infrastructure dependencies are not fully disclosed.

thesisQuality.basis: Strong enterprise adoption, $33.5B cRPO and rapid AI/data ARR growth support durable demand, but changing AI definitions and unisolated economics keep the assessment below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: 11% revenue growth, 14% CC cRPO growth, 20.5% GAAP operating margin and sharply higher quarterly cash flow are strong; acquisition contribution reduces organic clarity.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September market capitalization near $196B-$200B and about 27x trailing earnings against double-digit reported growth creates reasonable headroom, but acquisition-adjusted organic growth is lower and prevents an exceptional asymmetry conclusion.

catalystScore.basis: Organic reacceleration, AI/data adoption and acquisition integration are identifiable catalysts with near/medium-term reporting checkpoints, though integration and metric-definition uncertainty remain.

governancePower.basis: Large capital-return program and disclosed guidance decomposition support adequate capital allocation/transparency, while acquisition-heavy strategy introduces integration and allocation risk.

alignment2036.basis: Enterprise data, workflow automation and agent infrastructure address durable productivity and digital-infrastructure needs across many industries.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Sales, service, data, Slack and acquired data/agent capabilities reuse a common enterprise customer and workflow base, providing multiple demand engines.

bottleneckControl.basis: Embedded CRM data, permissions and workflows create switching friction, but external orchestration and model commoditization prevent treating Salesforce as an irreplaceable bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Recurring enterprise software, broad workflow coverage and cash generation support resilience, offset by acquisition execution and AI-platform substitution risk.

substitutionResilience.basis: Installed workflow/data context raises replacement friction, while hyperscalers, point automation and portable agent orchestration remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Software delivery avoids many physical supply constraints and Salesforce has broad platform scope, but current evidence does not establish exceptional redundancy across cloud/model infrastructure dependencies.

pricingPower.basis: 20.5% GAAP operating margin, 34.1% non-GAAP margin and expanding premium agentic SKUs support meaningful value capture, but direct price-pass-through evidence is limited.

riskEvidence.basis: Principal risks are acquisition-heavy growth quality, evolving AI metric definitions and potential value migration to external orchestration; none currently invalidate the thesis but they materially constrain confidence.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Recent primary operating evidence and independent current market valuation are available with exact lineage; confidence is reduced for undisclosed Agentforce unit economics and limited independent corroboration of issuer-specific operating metrics.

scoreRecord.thesis: Salesforce combines a deeply embedded enterprise CRM/data/workflow estate with rapidly scaling agentic products, creating durable automation leverage, while valuation and organic-growth quality remain constrained by acquisition contribution and evolving AI metrics.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: AI economics may prove less incremental than headline ARR suggests while acquisitions obscure organic growth and external orchestration reduces platform differentiation.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 FY27 results and subsequent disclosures separating organic growth, Agentforce economics and acquisition contribution.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore records the methodology-weighted component score less the locked risk penalty; data confidence is separately retained for downstream confidence treatment.
